capabilities: Browse a gallery of 13,561 real designs across 184 categories with search and collections
Look up 62 UI components with live specimens, plain-language explanations, and AI prompts
Study 44 visual styles with recognition signals and pasteable style briefs
Practice naming designs with a spaced-repetition aesthetic quiz
Generate replication prompts for coding agents and save ratings, tags, and notes as Markdown
disambiguation: Not a UI component library or theme; it is a study and reference tool for learning interface design.
extras: Fully bilingual Chinese/English; all data is bundled in main.js so only three files need installing. Gallery thumbnails load from an external CDN; dictionary and style content is adapted from third-party sites (Kombai, namethatui.com) and the plugin is not affiliated with them.
motivation: The author says the hard part of building interfaces is usually not making them but being unable to name what you see or know what good looks like, so the plugin puts browsing, naming, note-taking, and quizzing in one tab.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to study UI design: builders often cannot name the patterns they see or recognize what good design looks like.

relations.evidence: The gallery catalogue and thumbnails come from Kombai Gallery
the dictionary and style atlas are adapted from namethatui.com via joeseesun/learnui

summary: UI design learning toolkit with a 13,500-design gallery, bilingual component dictionary, 44-style atlas, spaced-repetition quiz, and copyable AI replication prompts.
